audits.title: Organisation of services for acute stroke in Scotland--report of the Scottish stroke services audit.
audits.standard: Key recommendations of the four SIGN stroke guidelines (14 key components of an integrated stroke service)
audits.setting: 43 Trusts, three directly managed units and 15 Health Boards providing or commissioning in-patient stroke care in Scotland

cycle1.result: No Trust provided all 14 key components; lack of provision was widespread for fast-track TIA/minor stroke clinics and CT scanning within 48 hours.

audits.other_findings: Provision varied between Trusts of similar and different sizes; Health Boards were at an early stage of stroke service specifications.
audits.citation: Roberts MA, Allen A, Langhorne P, McEwen J, D'A Semple P. Organisation of services for acute stroke in Scotland--report of the Scottish stroke services audit. Health Bull (Edinb). 2000;58(2):87-95. PMID: 12813835.

audits.title: Stroke units: research and reality. Results from the National Sentinel Audit of Stroke.
audits.standard: Five key organisational characteristics of stroke units from research literature; National Service Framework for Older People target of a stroke unit in all hospitals by April 2004
audits.setting: 240 hospitals in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (2001-2 National Sentinel Audit of Stroke)

cycle1.result: 73% of hospitals had a stroke unit but only 36% of admissions spent any time on one; 46% of stroke units had all five key characteristics, 26% had four and 28% three or fewer.

audits.other_findings: Better organisation was associated with better process of care.
audits.citation: Rudd AG, Hoffman A, Irwin P, Pearson M, Lowe D, Intercollegiate Working Party for Stroke. Stroke units: research and reality. Results from the National Sentinel Audit of Stroke. Qual Saf Health Care. 2005;14(1):7-12. doi:10.1136/qshc.2004.011031. PMID: 15691997.

audits.title: Hospital management and outcomes of stroke in Indigenous Australians: evidence from the 2009 Acute Care National Stroke Audit.
audits.standard: National Stroke Audit clinical processes of care (e.g. stroke unit care, timely allied health assessment)
audits.setting: 33 hospitals in the 2009 National Stroke Audit (acute services)

cycle1.result: 7% Indigenous; Indigenous patients less likely to receive stroke unit care and timely allied health assessment.

audits.other_findings: Indigenous patients aged 18-64 had threefold odds of death or dependency at discharge (aOR 3.09, 95% CI 1.07-8.95).
audits.citation: Kilkenny MF, Harris DM, Ritchie EA, Price C, Cadilhac DA, National Stroke Foundation. Hospital management and outcomes of stroke in Indigenous Australians: evidence from the 2009 Acute Care National Stroke Audit. Int J Stroke. 2013;8(3):164-171. doi:10.1111/j.1747-4949.2011.00717.x. PMID: 22299773.

audits.title: New Zealand National Acute Stroke Services Audit: acute stroke care delivery in New Zealand.
audits.standard: Acute stroke care quality indicators (stroke unit care, thrombolysis, anticoagulation in AF, aspirin, therapy assessments)
audits.setting: 20 of 21 District Health Boards, national audit

cycle1.result: Only 28% managed in a stroke unit; 38% arrived within 4.5 hours but only 3% thrombolysed; of 40% with known AF, only 24% were taking anticoagulants.

audits.other_findings: Stroke unit patients had higher thrombolysis rates, faster MDT assessment and less stroke progression (8% vs 15%); acute aspirin use and speech language therapy assessments also need improvement.
audits.citation: Child N, Fink J, Jones S, Voges K, Vivian M, Barber PA. New Zealand National Acute Stroke Services Audit: acute stroke care delivery in New Zealand. N Z Med J. 2012;125(1358):44-51. PMID: 22864156.

audits.title: Twenty years of monitoring acute stroke care in Australia through the national stroke audit programme (1999-2019): A cross-sectional study.
audits.setting: National Stroke Audit, up to 197 hospitals

cycle1.result: Thrombolysis 3%, stroke unit access 52%, risk factor advice 40%, carer training 24%; stroke unit access at hospitals 42% (1999)

audits.intervention: Repeated national audit cycles with feedback

cycle2.result: Thrombolysis 11%, stroke unit access 69%, risk factor advice 63%, carer training 51%; hospital stroke unit access 81%, thrombolysis services 85%

audits.citation: Purvis T, Cadilhac DA, Hill K, Reyneke M, Olaiya MT, Dalli LL, et al.. Twenty years of monitoring acute stroke care in Australia through the national stroke audit programme (1999-2019): A cross-sectional study. J Health Serv Res Policy. 2023;28(4):252-261. doi:10.1177/13558196231174732. PMID: 37212454.
